storyboard.claim: Luther's courage starts an immediate ripple effect in the room.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the ripple of reaction across the council.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the crisis to the reaction it causes.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the consequence of the declaration.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the ripple is the reaction, carried by the words.

storyboard.claim: Remis Corwo steps up when Luther speaks, though he tried to warn him off.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the council, where Reis rises to speak.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the next actor in the scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the father's reversal from warning to backing.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the reversal is named, the father is not drawn.

storyboard.claim: Reis tells the council their ancestors did not choose the phoenix sigil for the house to cower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for Reis's public statement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives Reis's words as the turn.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phrase carries the house's pride in its sigil.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the house's pride is in the words, no icon fits the phoenix.

storyboard.claim: Luther ties the survival of all half mortals to Diem's reign.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the wager he makes for his people.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the stake of the bond.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the wager in plain words.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the wager is the words, the stake is the reign.

storyboard.claim: Dictating a continent's fate traces back to the original sins of this world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for the temple on Corel, where the history is revealed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the scene back to the island of Corel.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links the bond to the world's first crime.
storyboard.staging: Callout on the stage: the return to Corel is the words, the temple is the place.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred are ancient, godlike beings who shaped the world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A wide sky over the Realm of Light and Shadow with the name of the Kindred.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the Kindred amid the fire.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the Kindred have no drawable figure in the cast; the callout alone names them.
storyboard.staging: Empty wide frame with the callout naming the Kindred.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred are weeping and confessing their most shameful sin to Diem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The temple stage with the confession named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The Kindred now speak after the battle.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the weeping cannot be drawn; the callout carries the confession.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with callout; no figure drawn, the words carry the confession.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred built the temple on Corel out of god stone, with no malice intended.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The temple on Corel where the god stone was used.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the origin of the god stone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the object the temple is built from: the god stone.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with the callout naming the god stone temple.

storyboard.claim: A child cut his hand on the god stone in a tragic accident.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The temple stage where the accident happened, named by the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The monument's intention is followed by its accident.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the accident concrete: a child, a hand, the stone.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with the callout; no medical icon, which would read as care.

storyboard.claim: The god stone material was highly toxic and lethal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The temple stage with the warning named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The accident reveals the stone's danger.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the property of the material that the monument hid.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with callout; no icon, since no icon reads toxicity literally.

storyboard.claim: Umbrose magic, which works on shadows in the mind, wiped the memory of Ofuca and the stone's danger from everyone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract set with the magic named in the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the method of the erasure.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no icon reads shadow-magic literally; the callout names the method.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with callout; no icon, so no false reading.

storyboard.claim: They erased their own brother from history because they were terrified.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract set with the erasure named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the judgement with the concrete victim.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the erased brother cannot be drawn; the callout names who was erased.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with callout naming the erased brother.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred feared the mortals would harvest the god stone and wipe out the children.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract set with the fear named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the motive for the erasure.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the fear; no face of fear can be drawn for the Kindred.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with the fear callout.

storyboard.claim: Diem did the same thing: when Luther was dying of god stone poisoning, she acted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther fallen on the floor, eyes shut, from the poisoning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recalls the earlier scene where Luther was poisoned.
storyboard.addedInformation: Collapsed reads as fallen and dying, not as treatment.
storyboard.staging: Luther collapsed on the floor, sad: the dying man Diem is recalling.

storyboard.claim: Diem vowed never to harm mortals, but at the brink of death she did.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther fallen on the floor again, at the brink of death.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Luther memory with Diem's vow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Repeats the collapse so the viewer links the vow to Luther's fall.
storyboard.staging: Luther collapsed, sad, with the callout on the brink of death.

storyboard.claim: Diem sank a blade into mortal flesh, breaking her own code to save Luther.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract set with the act named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the act Diem committed to save Luther.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no blade icon exists; the callout names the act.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with the callout on the blade.

storyboard.claim: The different types of bonds show up in the chaos at the temple.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The temple stage with the chaos named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the theory of bonds to the battle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the next argument at the temple.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with callout on the chaos.

storyboard.claim: True power is not about controlling others like chess pieces.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Abstract set with the rejected phrase struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects control as the source of power.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the phrase the narrator rejects.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with the struck phrase, no figure staged controlling.

storyboard.claim: Diem takes the velvety rose bane petal, a hallucinogenic, highly toxic poison lethal even to the descended.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Forest set with the poison named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to Diem's earlier action.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the petal cannot be drawn; the callout names it.
storyboard.staging: Forest set with callout on the rose bane poison.

storyboard.claim: She knows the danger and swallows it anyway, and she is not being mind controlled.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Abstract set with the rejected phrase struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the control reading of Diem's act.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the mind-control reading; no icon, since puppeteer would show control.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with struck callout; no figure is staged as controlled.

storyboard.claim: The hosts now argue the opposing side for a moment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Temple stage with the turn named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the counterargument that Ofus is superior.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the counterargument to come.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with the devil's advocate callout.

storyboard.claim: Ofus's method looks superior: he is the ultimate tactician holding every card.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy on the temple stage: his method reads as the winning side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the devil's-advocate turn: the case for Ofus.
storyboard.addedInformation: Trophy reads status and winning, which is the tactician claim.
storyboard.staging: No cast; the trophy alone carries the winner's status.

storyboard.claim: A red-haired old god, forgotten by the modern world, sits by the roots.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Forest set with no figure: the god is not in the cast.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the figure at the roots of the tree from 211.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the god is not drawn; only the callout names him.
storyboard.staging: Empty forest frame; the callout speaks.

storyboard.claim: The peace is real and Diem deserves it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy: a reward earned.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the case from 220 for her rest.
storyboard.addedInformation: Trophy reads a reward, matching deserves.
storyboard.staging: No cast; trophy icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: The host says to let her rest, the same way he felt reading it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon: a banter line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host sides with Diem before the turn.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: banter carries only the callout.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: Step back and view the story with a critical, cynical eye.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon: the callout names the stance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pivot from the story to the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a stance has no literal icon.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: Does the bond make Diem and Luther really terrible leaders?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther thinking, troubled by the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the summary in 234 into the question.
storyboard.addedInformation: worried with think avoids the shocked read of worried with talk.
storyboard.staging: Luther thinks with a worried face.

storyboard.claim: The test is a tiny cut on Luther's hand, and his reaction is the question.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther on screen, deciding, with no icon: a cut is not drawn because blood reads as harm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the test proposal from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the cut itself is only spoken, not shown.
storyboard.staging: Luther, worried, considers the proposed cut on his own hand.

storyboard.claim: The chance of Luther being incapacitated when Diem needs him is reckless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther alone, uneasy, with no literal icon for a risk to his health.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the reason for the refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the risk of incapacitation is not drawn, only judged.
storyboard.staging: Luther, worried, reflects on the risk to himself.

storyboard.claim: The critique is the fairest a reader could make, and it makes them flawed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther speaking, neutral, with no icon: the critique is carried by the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the critique of the generals.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the fairness of the critique is only spoken.
storyboard.staging: Luther, neutral, talks while the callout carries the judgment.

storyboard.claim: The author's writing lifts the whole genre.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host-only beat with no figure: the callout carries the claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the critique to the writing's achievement.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no picture of the writing itself; the callout is the content.
storyboard.staging: No character on screen; the callout speaks.

storyboard.claim: The same flaw lets them break the millennia-long cycle of violence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther speaking, neutral, with no literal icon for a broken cycle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the flaw into the reason for the reframing.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no icon can draw a cycle breaking without reading as a crack or chains.
storyboard.staging: Luther talks while the callout names the cycle being broken.

storyboard.claim: Someone has to pay the terrible price for Diem's third choice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther thinking, worried, with no icon: the question is the content.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the law into the open question.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the payer is not shown; the question stays open.
storyboard.staging: Luther, worried, thinks about who must pay.
